probes.question: What was the South Sea Company created in 1711 to do?
options: Reduce the size of public debts

probes.question: True or false: Isaac Newton lost at least £10,000 in South Sea stock.

image.alt: An 18th-century satirical print titled Bubble Cards showing speculators climbing a tree and others tumbling into the sea, with a verse about South Sea speculation
image.credit: Scanned from reprint of 1841/1852 editions of "Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds" by Charles Mackay, LL. D. ISBN 1-5866-3558-1 / Wikimed

panels.text: The South Sea Company was founded in 1711 to reduce the size of public debts. In 1720, its stock peaked, then collapsed in what became the South Sea Bubble.
Sir Isaac Newton owns nearly £22,000 in South Sea stock, and loses at least £10,000.
He is quoted: "I can calculate the movement of the stars, but not the madness of men".
